top_signals.title: Oil Prices Slide Despite Mounting Threats in the Strait of Hormuz
top_signals.summary: Crude oil prices moved lower in early Asian trading on Wednesday, extending the recent downward trend despite reports of increasingly frequent incidents involving tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian authorities attributing them to mines and other sources suggesting strikes with projectiles. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $90.10 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $80.71, after the American Petroleum Institute reported a modest build in U.S. crude oil inventories, at 126,000 barrels for the week to November…

top_signals.title: UK Energy Price Cap Jumps 26% in January, Highest Since 2023
top_signals.summary: Energy prices for UK households will surge by 26% from January 1 as the Middle East war is pushing wholesale gas prices higher, the UK’s energy regulator Ofgem said in its quarterly energy cap announcement on Wednesday. The UK has a so-called Energy Price Cap in place, which protects households from excessively high bills by capping the price that energy utility providers can pass on to them. The price cap is a limit on what suppliers can charge domestic consumers per kilowatt-hour of energy used. Every three months, the regulator reviews…

top_signals.title: Tech Selloff Rolls On as AI Worries Persist
top_signals.summary:
A global selloff in technology stocks is showing no sign of letting up as questions about the outlook for artificial intelligence pile up, with investors turning to bonds for safety. While technology stocks underperformed in Europe, the region’s greater exposure to defensive and cyclical stocks pushed the Stoxx 600 higher.

The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Anna Edwards, Guy Johnson and Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)
